- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is below recent highs, model tends to underreact — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent lows, model tends to overreact — adjust downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true peak) — apply 50% discount to forecasted peak if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if sentiment is mixed or negative, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.4 → +0.6), model tends to miss the reversal — adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment shift direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to anticipate rebound — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment turns positive within next 5 days.
